disputed.finding: “Parties must communicate an NDC every five years” is accurate only for the Article 4(9) cycle, but the draft could mislead by not noting that the first communication timing is handled elsewhere in Article 4; the notes only support the five-year repetition language, not a universal first-deadline rule as written.
disputed.objection: The draft only says NDCs are communicated every five years, per Article 4(9), and makes no claim about a first-deadline rule, so the finding objects to something the draft does not say.

disputed.finding: “The Paris Agreement’s central temperature goal is to keep warming well below 2°C ... while pursuing efforts to limit warming to 1.5°C” is accurate, but the draft slightly overstates this as “for all Parties together” without clarifying that Article 2 frames a collective global aim rather than a country-by-country binding ceiling.
disputed.objection: The draft explicitly states the goal is collective and not a country-specific limit, so the claimed overstatement is not present.

disputed.finding: The "Article 4(9)" quote uses an ellipsis that hides "in accordance with decision 1/CP.21 and any relevant decisions of the CMA". The draft therefore presents it as a self-contained treaty rule, and the cycle is in fact partly set by COP decisions.
disputed.objection: The notes do show an ellipsis in the Article 4(9) quote, but they do not establish that the omitted text materially changes the meaning or that the draft incorrectly treats the provision as self-contained.

disputed.finding: Today is Nov 2026. The draft describes the first stocktake only as a future schedule ("starting in 2023") and does not say it has concluded, that the next is due 2028, or that the NDCs informed by it were due in 2025. The framing is outdated.
disputed.objection: The notes do not discuss whether the draft is outdated as of Nov 2026 or whether later stocktakes/NDCs should have been mentioned, so this temporal criticism is unsupported by the notes.

disputed.finding: Article 14(3) does not itself mention NDCs. The draft's link from stocktake to NDCs rests on 4(9). It should say so, since the 14(3) quote is truncated and omits "in accordance with relevant provisions of this Agreement, as well as in enhancing international cooperation".
disputed.objection: Although the notes quote Article 14(3) as informing Parties in updating and enhancing actions and support, they do not show that the omission of the additional phrase materially misstates the treaty or that the draft needed the cross-reference to Article 4(9).
